result.title: MAGIC: Modality-Aware Gini Inspection for Clinical Hallucination Detection in LMMs
result.summary: Recent advances in medical large multimodal models (LMMs) have brought promising progress to clinical decision support, yet hallucination, the generation of confident but clinically unverifiable outputs, poses a critical threat to the reliability demanded in high-stakes medical settings. Existing hallucination detection methods, predominantly designed for unimodal settings, fail to capture the visual-linguistic dynamics inherent to medical imaging. We formulate the problem of hallucination detection in LMMs as disproportionate distribution of attention weights across the modalities during answer token generation. We quantify modality-specific attention concentration across layers and heads using the Gini coefficient and demonstrate statistically significant redistribution of attention mass between visual and textual tokens in hallucinated responses. We leverage these features to train a logistic regression-based classifier and evaluate it on two medical LMMs across three medical imaging modalities, demonstrating that our method achieves competitive or superior performance against contemporary hallucination detection baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把医学 LMM 的幻觉检测表述为生成答案 token 时视觉与文本模态间注意力权重的失衡，用 Gini 系数逐层逐头量化模态特定注意力集中度，发现幻觉回答中注意力质量在视觉与文本 token 间显著重分配，并据此训练逻辑回归分类器，在两个医学 LMM、三种影像模态上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 逐层逐头的视觉/文本注意力集中度可作为「答案是否真正使用视觉证据」的轻量诊断信号，与视觉旁路、信息坍缩及 latent 相似度中注意力结构的分析线索直接相关，但分类器是否具因果解释力仍需核查。
